title: Sequenced private upgrade automation and rollback lab
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Build a hardened automation and validation harness for sequenced upgrades of Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that performs orchestrated migrations with transactional safety, cohort-based canaries, and automatic rollback. This work combines an operator/controller to drive upgrade cohorts, a dry-run/tiered execution mode for schema and data migrations, and an upgrade 'lab' for reproducible failure testing and runbook generation.
acceptance_criteria: Operator/controller (CRD) that accepts a sequenced upgrade plan and can drive cohort rollouts (canary -> staggered -> full)
A dry-run mode that executes schema & config migrations in simulation and emits deterministic preflight reports (no mutating writes)
Transactional migration runner that supports idempotent up/down steps and safe pause/resume semantics
Automated rollback when predefined SLO or validation gates fail (latency regression, error rates, data drift checks)
Playbook and runbook artifacts generated from lab runs, with reproducible repro steps and example PRs for on-call
End-to-end test harness that can repro common failure classes (network partition, partial schema apply, KV cache mismatch) in CI with <30m median run time
plan_steps: Design CRD and controller lifecycle: plan spec, cohort definition, hooks (preflight/postflight/validate)
Implement dry-run engine: migration plan parser + simulator that validates state transitions without mutating DBs
Build transactional migration runner with snapshot/checkpoint support and idempotent migrations
Integrate telemetry hooks: emit upgrade events to telemetry pipeline (events: preflight, cohort-start, cohort-complete, validation-fail)
Create lab harness: toolbox to inject failures and run reproducible scenarios; tie to CI and internal QA
Documentation: Confluence runbook, CLI docs, sample upgrade plan templates and recommended gates
Iterate with Solutions and SREs on runbook slates and manual recovery flows
notes: Trade-offs: strong preference for transactional, idempotent migrations over fragile multi-step scripts; larger initial engineering cost but fewer customer incidents
Decision: use operator CRD + controller pattern (Kubernetes) for VPC and on-prem managed customers; also expose standalone CLI for air-gapped installs
Consideration: not all customers can take DB snapshots; runner must support incremental, reversible schema ops where possible
Rollout policy: default cohort sizes will be conservative (5% -> 25% -> 100%), with an explicit fast-path for emergency patches
Safety: include preflight static analysis (schema compatibility, migration time estimate) and dynamic probes (smoke RPCs + perf probes)
risks: Long-running migrations can cause KV cache divergence leading to increased latency; mitigation: prevalidate KV compatibility and provide rolling cache flush hooks
Customers with strict change windows may need manual override; mitigation: 'manual-approve' gate in plan spec
Operator/controller may not be supported in some on-prem environments; mitigation: provide CLI-first fallback with same core primitives
